TianshanOS API User Guide

Connect your own scripts and systems to monitor the device, control its computers, receive live status, run remote tasks, and maintain configuration and updates. This guide assumes familiarity with HTTP, JSON, and basic server operations; circuit and firmware knowledge is not required.

This guide is based on TianshanOS 0.6.4.

Find your task

TaskStart here
Make your first API callQuick start
Identify the controller and the two computersDevices and names
Monitor temperatures, fans, power, and computersMonitoring
Switch power or the USB connectionDevice control
Start and verify a remote serviceRemote tasks
Configure variables, sources, actions, and rulesAutomation and Configuration models
Transfer files or update firmwareMaintenance and Transfers
Receive live status and resultsWebSocket
Look up an APIComplete reference
Investigate errors or maintain a long-running integrationTroubleshooting and Operations

Reading order

Complete a read-only request in the quick start first. Then follow the scenario for your task, including its result checks and recovery steps. Open the reference when you need individual parameters.

The documented default accounts admin / root and initial password rm01 are product defaults. Other addresses, filenames, tokens, and response values are illustrative. Use the actual address and current password of a device you manage. Examples contain no private tokens, changed passwords, or real application records.

The reference covers 277 registered names in 28 functional groups, including config.pack.apply, which is retained but does not apply generic configuration. Dedicated file / image routes and WebSocket messages have separate chapters. A registered name does not guarantee that the required hardware, storage, credentials, or remote service is ready.

Quick start

Connect, log in, and read a protected measurement. Apart from creating and closing a login session, this sequence only reads status.

Set the device address

Use the device's current IP address. WebUI and business APIs use HTTP port 80 by default, so no explicit port is normally needed. The API prefix is /api/v1. Replace the example address with your own device address:

export TS_BASE='http://10.10.99.97'

For connection problems, check the IP address, network, and service state. See Troubleshooting.

Read controller information

curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/system/info"

Illustrative response excerpt:

{"code":0,"data":{"app":{"name":"TianShanOS","version":"0.6.4","compile_date":"Nov 5 2026","compile_time":"10:00:00"},"chip":{"model":"ESP32-S3","cores":2},"uptime_ms":123456}}

Check HTTP status and then code. Version is at data.app.version; uptime_ms is milliseconds. Do not assume a top-level data.version field.

Log in and retain the session

The default accounts are admin and root, both with initial password rm01. Log in and use the APIs permitted for that account. If you have changed the password, use your current password.

Set umask 077 before creating login.json and restrict access to the file. This example uses the default admin account:

{"username":"admin","password":"rm01"}
umask 077
curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @login.json \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/auth/login" > login-response.json
export TS_TOKEN="$(python3 -c 'import json; r=json.load(open("login-response.json")); assert r["code"] == 0; print(r["data"]["token"])')"

Successful data contains token, session_id, username, level, expires_in in seconds, and password_changed. Use token as the credential; session_id is only an identifier.

Use the returned token for subsequent calls. Access follows data.level and endpoint authorization. Password changes are an optional account-management operation through auth.change_password.

Handle password files, login responses, and tokens as credentials. Remove temporary credential files after use.

Read a protected temperature

curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/temp/read"

Illustrative excerpt:

{"code":0,"data":{"temperature_c":42.5,"temperature_01c":425,"source":"variable","timestamp_ms":120000,"valid":true}}

temperature_c is Celsius; temperature_01c is tenths of a degree. Only use the reading as valid when valid:true. Missing or invalid data must not become 0 degrees in your monitoring system.

Log out

curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \
  -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/auth/logout"
unset TS_TOKEN

POST logout returns {"success":true}, rather than the usual code / data envelope. Scripts and connections using the session need a valid session again.

Next, choose a task scenario or use the read-only Python example supplied with the editable documentation.

Devices and names

TianshanOS manages both its controller and the connected computers. Identify the target before calling an API: their status values describe different things.

User-facing nameAPI identifierPurpose
Management controllersystem.*TianshanOS version, memory, tasks, and controller restart
Inference computerdevice:"agx"Power state, power control, and reset; monitor.* provides compute telemetry
Application computerdevice:"lpmu"Power state, power control, reset, and upper-level network access setup
Cooling fansfan.* and numeric idRPM, control mode, temperature curve, and output limits
Touch light, board light, matrix displaytouch, board, matrixColors, effects, images, QR codes, and text
Local storage/sdcard/... and other supported pathsFiles, configuration packages, and supported update materials
Remote hostSaved SSH host id / hostServer commands or managed processes; not necessarily one of the built-in computers

Use agx and lpmu exactly as the API identifiers. For example, the application computer is still addressed as {"device":"lpmu"}.

Interpret measurements correctly

  • Fan duty is the output percentage, from 0 to 100. RPM is rotational speed. Unknown duty may be null; also check duty_valid.
  • Temperature source may be a local sensor, compute telemetry, a variable, or a manual test value. Check the source, valid flag, and timestamp.
  • power_good is a hardware power indication. It does not establish that the operating system or application is ready.
  • USB target selects a shared USB route. Switching it can interrupt traffic on the previous route.
  • run_id identifies a managed remote service run. A retained record does not establish that its process is still running; verify its status.
  • Operation receipt contains an operation identifier and result credentials. Preserve the complete receipt rather than just a display name.

Three stages of completion

  1. The API accepts the request, for example by returning started:true.
  2. The device action or remote process reaches the requested state.
  3. Your application becomes ready, for example by passing a health check.

Confirm the stage your task requires. Restarting the controller, powering a computer, and starting its application are separate operations.

Task scenarios

Examples use TS_BASE and TS_TOKEN from the quick start. Replace addresses, object IDs, configuration versions, and receipts with actual values. Control examples have real effects: use only the task you intend to perform.

Monitor the device

Read temperatures, cooling, power, and computer status into your monitoring system. Log in for READ capabilities; some overview endpoints are public.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" "$TS_BASE/api/v1/temp/read"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" "$TS_BASE/api/v1/fan/status"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" "$TS_BASE/api/v1/power/status"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" "$TS_BASE/api/v1/device/status?device=agx"

Retain temperature valid, fan duty_valid, power valid / crc_valid, and last update times. Display invalid or disconnected states explicitly. duty is a percentage; rpm is rotational speed. Computer state=on does not establish application readiness. See Response models.

Successful monitoring means valid readings that keep updating. Use WebSocket for a continuous dashboard. For invalid temperatures, inspect temp.sources; for compute telemetry problems, inspect monitor.status. Do not replace missing values with zero. The supplied Python example performs login, reads, and logout only.

Control a computer

ADMIN is required. First read device.status to identify agx or lpmu and its current state. Use an explicit on / off action rather than repeating toggle after a timeout.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{"device":"agx","action":"on"}' \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/device/power"

Then GET device.status and inspect state / power_good. Confirm application readiness on the target computer or through a business health endpoint. For normal shutdown use off. force_off / reset interrupt work and can lose data; arrange target-system maintenance first.

Operational note

To switch USB, POST device.usb.set with {"target":"agx"}, then GET device.usb.status. Other targets are esp32 / lpmu / disconnect. The old route may disconnect during the switch; that alone is not a device fault.

After a timeout, query state before retrying. Preserve error state, power indication, and details if the target does not reach the expected state.

Adjust lights and fans

Routine LED operations need ADMIN. GET led.list to obtain a device name, then fill it:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{"device":"board","color":"#00A0FF"}' \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/led/fill"

Read led.list again. To use the display after restart, separately POST led.save with {"device":"board"} and inspect saved. Displaying and saving startup settings are different steps.

For fans, read fan.status / config first. POST fan.set with {"id":0,"duty":50} only after obtaining the actual fan ID. fan.mode selects off / manual / auto / curve. Curve, limits, and persistence permissions are listed in the Fan reference.

Check duty_valid / duty / target_duty, temperature, and faults after changing output. Restore the intended control mode after a temporary manual setting.

Manage remote tasks

Use ssh.exec / exec_stream for a one-off command; use a saved SSH command and run record for a continuously managed service. Raw command execution requires ROOT; starting an existing managed service requires at least ADMIN.

Operational note

Before starting, confirm reachability, a verified host fingerprint, and a saved host referencing a valid SSH key. Unknown / changed fingerprints are verified through ssh.test and trusted information, not by clearing trust or automatically accepting.

  1. With root, read ssh.hosts and ssh.commands. Check host, command, service_mode, and readiness matching. See Configuration models.
  2. Read the latest active_version and start the saved service:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{"command_id":"YOUR_SERVICE_COMMAND_ID","active_version":"CURRENT_VERSION"}' \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/ssh/services/start"
  1. Retain run_id and operation_id. POST automation.services.status with {"run_id":"YOUR_RUN_ID","verify":true}. Inspect operation_phase, busy, and state. verify connects to the original host; it is not just a local cache read.
  2. Verify application health / readiness. To stop, POST automation.services.stop with the original run_id and continue querying status.

A run_id is not a ready indication; last_known is a previous observation. Deleting configuration or a local key does not stop remote processes. Use the original run identity rather than guessing a process by name.

For a one-off stream, authenticate WebSocket before POST ssh.exec_stream. Keep the complete receipt and use ssh.exec_status after interruption. Never rerun a command merely to retrieve missing output. See Streaming SSH for execution, matching, and output completeness.

Configure automation

The flow is: acquire data, map it into variables, then execute an action when conditions hold. With root, read automation.status / config.status first. Resolve loading, enablement, pause, or SD-source selection issues before editing.

Start with a saved user variable:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/automation/config/status"

Use its active_version in the next request:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{"name":"example.temperature","value":42.5,"active_version":"CURRENT_VERSION"}' \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/automation/variables/set"

Read automation.variables.get with root to confirm value, readonly, and source_id. Retain the new active_version. Create an enabled:false rule from the rule model; use a log action before adding power or remote-execution effects.

Add a real data source only when needed. Verify data arrival, variable updates, and stale status before enabling the rule. Saving a definition, enabling configuration, starting the engine, and executing actions are separate states; saved:true alone is insufficient.

Refresh and merge after a conflict. Preview deletion impact. Preview / apply SD or backup selection. Respect pause / busy results rather than overwriting managed files.

Maintain the device

Choose one maintenance goal at a time so its effects can be checked.

GoalSequenceCompletion
Back up an objectExport with the role required by that object; save tscfg; preview any later importComplete package retained and verifiable; export is not recovery
Save a fileUpload, inspect attributes, download and compareIntended path, length, and bytes
Update firmware / WWWCheck matching images, transfer, read global progress, confirm state, restart if neededCorrect running identity / version and working application
Change networkingRecord old access / configuration, change, save, reconnectManagement and target networking both work
Change a passwordchange_password, log in again, update client sessionsNew credentials work; old sessions are no longer assumed valid
Install identity certificateCheck CSR / key match, install, inspect cert.status and client trustCorrect material, actual loaded identity, and verified client connection

See Transfers and updates for complete requests and capacity limits. cert.* manages device identity, key.* manages SSH keys, and hosts.* manages remote fingerprints. After failure, establish which stages took effect before retrying or recovering.

Common calling rules

Paths and methods

Business URLs have the form http://10.10.99.97/api/v1/.... Dots in a logical name become path separators: fan.status maps to /api/v1/fan/status. Preserve case, including key.exportPrivate and log.setLevel.

Use only the methods listed for each API. Read operations usually allow GET / POST; writes usually allow POST / PUT / DELETE, with some POST-only endpoints. This guide generally uses GET for simple queries and POST for actions. A disallowed method returns HTTP405.

Names and parameters determine the action. Do not infer that DELETE always deletes an object or POST always creates one.

Sessions and roles

Protected requests carry Authorization: Bearer <token>. Do not place tokens in URLs. A role or session_id supplied in ordinary request JSON does not establish that identity.

Access labelMeaning
PublicThis capability can be accessed without login; resource conditions still apply
READAt least read permission; authorized admin / root sessions normally qualify
ADMINRoutine device operations; admin or root required
ROOTRaw command execution, automation definition writes, and selected account management; root required
Body tokenAuthentication APIs validate the token JSON field; this is not anonymous permission to change accounts

Default accounts are admin / root, both with initial password rm01. The policy distinguishes READ / WRITE / ADMIN / ROOT, but this does not imply an API for creating arbitrary accounts at all levels. No registered endpoint has minimum WRITE in this version.

Some resources or parameters add checks: ordinary file reads may allow READ; sensitive paths require ADMIN. config.get exposes only the language preference publicly; other keys require ADMIN. Full SSH host / command, rule, and action reads normally require ADMIN; secrets in automation.sources.list still require ROOT. temp.bind queries allow ADMIN, while binding changes require ROOT. automation.proxy.fetch inherits destination permissions for local APIs and requires ROOT for external services. restricted:true means fields were filtered; never save omitted fields back as empty values.

Parameters

Use Content-Type: application / json and a JSON object body. Arrays belong inside object fields. Avoid duplicate keys and overlapping query / body parameter names; conflicts are rejected.

Query values are decoded once and may be interpreted as integers or booleans. Prefer JSON for objects, arrays, floating-point values, null, and identifiers whose leading zeroes must be preserved. Do not URL-encode twice.

Optional means that omission is permitted; null is not generally equivalent to omission. Some binding APIs explicitly use null to clear a binding. Time units are field-specific: milliseconds, seconds, or Unix time.

Determine the result

Usual success:

{"code":0,"data":{"example":"value"}}

Business errors can still use HTTP200:

{"code":1,"error":"invalid_request"}

Explanations may be in error or message. data may be an object, an array, or absent. A successful response need not contain message.

  1. Handle non-success HTTP status as a transport, authorization, format, or service failure.
  2. If code is present and nonzero, handle a business error.
  3. Check the endpoint's valid, success, exit_code, persisted, or operation status. A top-level success does not replace these checks.
  4. For asynchronous work, use the completion flow specified by that API; retain a receipt when one is returned. After a disconnect or result_unknown, inspect state before retrying.

Login, logout, binary uploads, and downloads have dedicated formats. A successful download body contains file bytes, not JSON.

Error codes

codeNameSuggested response
0OKCheck the endpoint's completion conditions
1INVALID_ARGCheck fields, types, ranges, and version conditions
2NOT_FOUNDRefresh object / operation information; do not invent or reuse stale IDs
3NO_PERMISSIONCheck role, sensitive resources, and export conditions
4BUSYInspect active work and wait before retrying
5TIMEOUTDetermine whether a result exists before repeating a write
6NO_MEMReduce request size or load; preserve known results
7INTERNALRetain the reason; investigate state if result_unknown
8NOT_SUPPORTEDUse a supported entry point
9HARDWAREInspect the device, sensor, and configuration
10CONNECTIONCheck network, remote host, fingerprint, and service
11AUTHReauthenticate or complete the required verification

SSH trust flows also use1001/1002 for unknown / changed host fingerprints and provide fingerprint details. Verify through a trusted channel before confirming; deleting trust records is not identity verification.

Effects and persistence

applied reports an applied setting; persisted or saved reports storage success. They can differ. An error may occur after an earlier stage has taken effect: retain its details and read back state.

Toggles, rule triggers, remote execution, and updates are not guaranteed safe to repeat. Read-only queries may be retried with appropriate load control. After a write timeout, query state or the receipt first.

Limits

Connections, bodies, receive times, and task slots are bounded. Identity and size checks can reject a request before consuming its entire body. Avoid replacing live subscriptions with large numbers of concurrent polls.

This version allows up to 1 MiB for the generic JSON route with a30-second receive budget; authentication requests are limited to 16 KiB/10 seconds. Configuration packages themselves are limited to 64 KiB. Individual APIs can impose smaller limits. See Transfers for binary routes.

JSON nesting is limited to 32. Embedded NUL, trailing garbage, and duplicate keys are rejected. For HTTP413, reduce the request or use the feature's designated upload route.

Common response models

These fields are inside data. Handle HTTP status and code as described in Common rules. Fields vary with device state, initialization, and role. Preserve unknown when a field is missing; do not fill it with 0 or false.

temperature

FieldInterpretation
temperature_cCelsius. Both fields represent the same measurement.
temperature_01cTenths of a degree Celsius. The same measurement as temperature_c.
validWhether the value is usable; false must not be treated as normal temperature
sourceSource of this reading; interpretation depends on the API.
active_sourceActual source; interpretation depends on the API.
preferred_sourcePreferred source; interpretation depends on the API.
timestamp_ms, last_update_msMilliseconds since device start, not Unix time
stale, age_msStaleness / age in milliseconds; null may mean never updated
partial_stale, valid_count, stale_countPartial failure of a multi-variable binding; inspect more than its average

The implementation bounds valid temperature values. Inputs can come from local sensors, compute telemetry, variables, or manual tests. A manual value does not establish the physical temperature.

fan

fan.status returns a different shape depending on whether you supply id:

  • With id: one fan.
  • Without id: fans, plus temperature, temp_valid, and temp_source.
FieldType, unit, or meaning
idFan number.
modeControl mode: off, manual, auto, or curve.
duty_validWhether the output is valid.

target_dutyTarget output percentage; can differ from actual duty

control_temperatureControl temperature, in Celsius.
guard_temperatureProtection temperature, in Celsius.

temp_staleWhether temperature data is stale.

applied and persisted distinguish application from storage. Requesting 50% does not establish a valid physical 50% output.

power

power.status combines voltage, chip measurements, protection, and statistics. Use the specific voltage / chip/protection.status APIs for details.

FieldUnit or meaning
voltage_vVoltage, in V.

voltage_mvmV; convert before comparing to V

device.power.status reports measurements for individual power rails instead:

FieldMeaning
voltage_mvRail voltage, in mV.
current_maRail current, in mA.

Compute telemetry can also use mW. Follow each field's unit.

config-result

Configuration writes and source selection return a set of state flags; not every response contains all of them.

FieldMeaning

Preview package_digest and credential_generation are apply preconditions, not reusable global authorization. restart_required:false does not replace loaded/enabled or runtime checks.

variable

Variables include name and type/value_type. The following fields may also be present:

FieldMeaning
valueVariable value.

For variables.list, use include_value to request values and include_meta to request metadata. A missing value field is different from a null value.

certificate

cert.status reports the following separately:

FieldMeaning
has_private_keyWhether a private key is present.

HTTPS diagnostic-service statusStatus of the separate diagnostic service.

Certificate validity may depend on time_ready. An undetermined result must not be treated as valid.

An installed identity, the identity loaded by the separate HTTPS diagnostic service, and diagnostic-client trust are separate checks. Inspect service status after installation. Business APIs remain on HTTP; their Bearer roles are separate from mTLS certificate roles.

color

RGB components range from 0 to 255. Direct color APIs accept:

  • A supported color string.
  • An object with r, g, and b.
  • A decimal integer equivalent to 0xRRGGBB.

JSON does not allow hexadecimal numeric literals. led.color.hsv uses different ranges:

FieldMeaning
h0–359 degrees.
s, v0–255, not percentages.

Color correction is an object with the following structure:

FieldMeaning
enabledOverall enablement.
white_pointNested enabled, red_scale, green_scale, and blue_scale. Scales range from 0 to 2.
gammaNested enabled and gamma. The gamma range is 0.1–4.
brightness, saturationEach contains nested enabled and factor.

Send the corresponding nested objects when modifying them. Device brightness (0–255) and a correction factor use different units.

ota

After starting an update from a URL or SD, read ota.progress. It reports device-wide state; there is no private receipt for each login.

FieldMeaning
APP progressstate, percent, total_size, received_size, message.
WWW progressstate, percent, total, received, message, running.
  • APP: pending_reboot means a restart is needed.
  • WWW: completion is indicated by state=completed and running=false.

100 percent alone does not prove the new version is running.

Partition information includes:

FieldMeaning
label, address, sizePartition label, address, and size.
BootabilityWhether the partition is bootable.
version, projectVersion and project information, when available.
can_rollbackWhether rollback is currently available.

aborted acknowledges the cancellation call. Continue checking progress and actual state.

Binary uploads use a separate response. The following combination means that Flash was written but the SD recovery cache was not fully saved:

  • HTTP 409.
  • status=partial.
  • error=recovery_cache_failed.
  • flash_written=true.

Inspect partitions and recovery files before retrying.

network

Ethernet reports interface and configuration state separately:

FieldMeaning
interface_presentWhether the interface exists.
link_upPhysical link state.
config_error, config_error_nameConfiguration-application errors.

A connected cable does not establish that IP configuration succeeded.

Distinguish actual state, requested state, and the stage at which an error occurred:

FieldMeaning
DHCP runningActual state.
Ethernet want_runningRequested state.
restore_errorConfiguration-restoration error.
apply_errorConfiguration-application error.
resume_errorService-resumption error.

0 means that the corresponding step reported no error. Check the interface and link state before deciding whether the service should run.

Configuration models

These models save hosts, commands, sources, actions, and rules that the device can use at runtime. Save a disabled example and read it back before enabling effects.

Read the version before writing

With root, read automation.config.status and retain active_version. Put it at the top level of a write. After each successful write, use the new version for the next request. For rule updates, also carry the read revision as expected_revision. A conflict requires rereading and merging, not merely replacing the version token and replaying stale input.

The JSON objects below are complete request-shape examples. Replace CURRENT_VERSION, identifiers, addresses, keys, and variable names. Place model fields at the request top level; do not add a config wrapper except for explicitly shown subobjects.

restricted:true can indicate a metadata-only view. Use ADMIN for complete SSH host / command, rule, and action reads; automation.sources.list secrets still require ROOT. Writing definitions follows each endpoint's required role. Omitted secret fields are not empty values. Host / source updates merge with existing JSON; command / action updates should carry complete definitions. Rules use their own merge / revision checks; do not generalize one family's update behavior.

SSH hosts

For ssh.hosts.add / update. This records where / how to connect and which key to use; hosts.* stores fingerprints instead.

{"id":"example-host","active_version":"CURRENT_VERSION","host":"192.0.2.20","port":22,"username":"YOUR_USER","auth_type":"key","keyid":"example-key","enabled":true}
FieldType, limit, and meaning
idStable string, at most 31 bytes; must not already exist for add; must exist for update
hostAddress string, at most 63 bytes
portSSH integer port, normally22; use1-65535
usernameRemote user, at most 31 bytes; distinct from device login
auth_typekey / password; key is recommended for persistent definitions
keyidSaved local SSH private-key ID, at most 31 bytes
enabledBoolean, decoding default true
created_timeOptional unsigned 32-bit time value; normally retain the existing value

The persistent model does not store a password field. password mode does not imply a saved remote password; immediate calls supply their own credentials. At most16 hosts. Address, key existence, and remote trust are checked separately.

SSH commands

For ssh.commands.add / update. Saving does not execute a command. Use service_mode:false for short commands; managed long-running services use true and ssh.services.start.

{"id":"example-command","active_version":"CURRENT_VERSION","host_id":"example-host","name":"Read OS","command":"uname -a","timeout_sec":30,"enabled":true,"service_mode":false}
FieldType, limit, and meaning
id / host_idStrings, at most 31 bytes each; host_id references a saved host
name / commandStrings, at most63 /1023 bytes
desc / iconOptional strings, at most127 /63 bytes; icon can be a display icon or path
expect_pattern / fail_pattern / extract_patternOptional match / extraction patterns, at most 127 bytes each
var_nameOptional result-variable prefix, at most 31 bytes
timeout_sec0-65535 seconds, default 30; not milliseconds
stop_on_match / nohup / enabled / service_modeBooleans; enabled defaults true, others false
ready_pattern / service_fail_patternService readiness / failure patterns, at most 127 bytes each
ready_timeout_sec / ready_check_interval_msIntegers0-65535, seconds / milliseconds respectively; configure deliberately for services
created_timeOptional unsigned 32-bit time value

Aliases are timeout, expectPattern, failPattern, extractPattern, varName, stopOnMatch, serviceMode, readyPattern, serviceFailPattern, readyTimeout, readyInterval. Prefer table names; avoid supplying both aliases. _object_id / runtime_instance represent persistent / runtime identity; retain returned values rather than inventing them. At most64 commands.

Data sources

For automation.sources.add / update. Sources acquire data and map it to variables used by rules.

{"id":"example-source","active_version":"CURRENT_VERSION","label":"Temperature","type":"rest","enabled":false,"poll_interval_ms":5000,"auto_discover":false,"rest_url":"https://example.com/status","rest_method":"GET","mappings":[{"path":"temperature","var":"compute.temperature"}]}
Shared fieldType and meaning
id / labelStrings, at most63 /47 bytes
typebuiltin / websocket / socketio / rest / variable strings, or corresponding integers0-4
enabled / auto_discoverBooleans; auto_discover defaults true; example explicitly disables it
poll_interval_msInteger0-4294967295 milliseconds; update behavior depends on type; zero is not unlimited sampling
mappingsAt most4: path up to 95 bytes, var up to 63 bytes, optional transform up to 63 bytes

Mapping path / var also accept json_path / var_name. The path locates a field in data, such as temperature or cpu.cores[0].freq; it is not a URL. Verify transforms with known sample values.

TypeType-specific fields
websocketws_uri up to 95 bytes; ws_path legacy single-field path up to 63 bytes; reconnect_ms0-65535 ms
socketiosio_url up to 95 bytes; sio_event up to 63 bytes
restrest_url up to 95 bytes; rest_method up to 7 bytes; rest_auth up to 47 bytes; rest_path legacy path up to 63 bytes
variablevar_name, var_prefix, var_watch_all; SSH data flows also use ssh_host_id, ssh_command, expect_pattern, fail_pattern, extract_pattern, timeout_sec
builtinbuiltin object: type selects a built-in sample; GPIO uses pin, ADC uses channel / atten, computer state can use device_index

String-type inputs also accept convenience aliases: WebSocket uri / json_path; Socket.IO url / event; REST url / method / auth_header / json_path. Prefer canonical fields above. Variable-source strings are generally at most 63 bytes, ssh_command 95 bytes, timeout_sec0-65535 seconds. For built-in numeric hardware type / channel IDs, start from existing definitions rather than guessing pins or channels.

User variables

automation.variables.set writes; get / list reads. Name, source, readonly, and age matter in addition to value.

{"name":"example.temperature","value":42.5,"active_version":"CURRENT_VERSION"}

value supports null, boolean, finite number, or a string up to 63 bytes. Normally omit value_type for inference. Explicit types are0=null,1=bool,2=int,3=float,4=string and must match. Integers use signed 32-bit range; other finite numeric values use floating point.

source_id defaults to user. create_only:true preserves an existing variable, so it does not establish that the new requested value was written. Readonly / system-source variables can reject changes. Temperature binding requires suitable numeric temperature variables; strings, invalid values, and stale data are not normal sensor readings.

Action templates

automation.actions.add / update saves reusable actions. This example logs a message rather than controlling hardware.

{"id":"example-action","active_version":"CURRENT_VERSION","name":"Record a message","enabled":true,"type":"log","async":false,"delay_ms":0,"log":{"level":3,"message":"Example action"}}

Shared fields: id up to 63 bytes, name 47 bytes, description 63 bytes; enabled defaults true, async false; delay_ms0-65535 milliseconds. created_at is an optional nonnegative integer time value, normally retained from the existing object.

typeType-specific subobject and fields
loglog: level, message up to 47 bytes
set_varset_var: variable, value, optional value_type
ssh_cmdssh: host_ref, command, timeout_ms, async
ssh_cmd_refssh_ref: cmd_id referencing a saved command
gpiogpio: pin, level as a boolean, pulse_ms
device_ctrldevice: device, action using supported actions
clicli: command, var_name, timeout_ms
webhookwebhook: url, method, body_template
ledled: device, ctrl_type and fields for that display function

Host references, variable names, command references, and device / action names are generally up to 63 bytes. Inline SSH / CLI commands and webhook URL are up to 95 bytes, method 7 bytes, body_template 63 bytes. Overlong fields are rejected; do not rely on truncation. Inline action commands have less capacity than saved ssh.commands.

LED action fields

led.ctrl_type is fill / effect / brightness / off / text / image / qrcode / filter / filter_stop / text_stop. Supply fields for the chosen function, not every parameter from a direct LED API.

Shared display fields: device, index (255=all), color string or r / g / b, brightness0-255, effect, speed, duration_ms0-65535. Matrix fields: text up to 127 bytes, font31, image_path127, qr_text255, qr_ecc string L / M / Q / H, filter31, filter_params, center, loop, scroll, align, x / y, auto_pos for text positioning. scroll is none / left / right / up / down; align left / center / right; x / y signed 16-bit coordinates.

QR foreground uses qr_fg; background uses qr_bg_image. Explicit black is an intentional color, not an omitted value. filter_params uses named numeric options supported by the effect. Execution additionally requires supported hardware and valid paths / configuration. Save / read before deliberately testing an effect.

Automation rules

automation.rules.add / update saves conditions and actions. Enabled rules can begin executing automatically; initially set enabled:false.

{"id":"example-rule","active_version":"CURRENT_VERSION","name":"Temperature example","enabled":false,"logic":"and","cooldown_ms":10000,"conditions":[{"variable":"example.temperature","operator":"gt","value":50}],"actions":[{"type":"log","level":3,"message":"Temperature high"}]}
FieldType and meaning
id / name / iconStrings, at most63 /47 /63 bytes; ID rejects separators / control characters
enabledBoolean, default true; example explicitly disables it
manual_trigger / show_on_dashboard / allow_manual_triggerBooleans for triggering / presentation, not caller privilege
cooldown_msUnsigned 32-bit milliseconds
revisionRule revision; use read revision as expected_revision for update conditions
logic / conditionsand / or, default and; up to 255 conditions
actionsUp to 255 entries; enabled rule cannot have no actions

A condition is {variable, operator, value}; operators eq / ne / lt / le / gt / ge / contains. Values follow the variable model. conditions:{logic, items:[...]} is also accepted; choose one representation.

Inline rule actions use flat fields: log has level / message, SSH has host_ref / command, GPIO has pin / level. Templates use nested subobjects instead. Inline SSH type is ssh; template type is ssh_cmd. A template_id reference takes precedence over cached inline fields.

Shared action fields: delay_ms, async, repeat_mode (once / while_true / count), repeat_count0-255, repeat_interval_ms0-65535, optional condition (condition model; null clears it). Select repetition with the action's effects in mind.

Inline typeFlat fields
log / set_varlevel / message; or variable / value / value_type
ssh / ssh_cmd_refhost_ref / command / ssh_async / timeout_ms; or cmd_id
gpio / device_ctrlpin / boolean level / pulse_ms; or device / action
webhook / cliurl / method / body_template; or command / var_name / timeout_ms
ledFlat device / ctrl_type / r / g / b etc.; ctrl_type uses an integer enum rather than template strings

Prefer referencing a saved template for complex LED rules. Inline ctrl_type:0 fill,1 effect,2 brightness,3 off,4 text,5 image,6 qrcode,7 filter,8 filter_stop,9 text_stop. Inline qr_ecc is a character-code integer: L76 / M77 / Q81 / H72.

filter_params remains its own object. Integer ranges: speed1-100; intensity / density / decay / amplitude0-255; scale1-100; levels 2-16; amount / saturation / frequency0-100; angle0-360; width1-16; wavelength1-32. These template / UI units differ from some direct LED filter units. Do not place an entire API request into the actions array.

Module configuration

config.module.show returns the module's config object. Read existing fields before config.module.set changes one key. Modules: net / dhcp / wifi / nat / led / fan / device / system. See individual operations for all support. key is local to the module; preserve the value type.

config.module.save and dirty state are separate from automation active_version. Networking changes can interrupt access; record the access route first. WiFi views below ADMIN omit passwords.

Monitoring widgets

ui.widgets stores frontend layout JSON; it does not create collectors. widgets is a frontend-interpreted array and may initially be empty. Start from ui.widgets.get and retain existing fields / IDs. refresh_interval is milliseconds, default 5000. Whole serialized configuration is limited to 4000 bytes. nvs_saved does not imply that a variable has data.

Import, deletion, and source selection

Use preview then apply with the preview's preconditions. tscfg is complete package JSON as a string, not an arbitrary object. Hosts, commands, sources, and actions import use expected_digest / expected_credential. Rule import has different confirmation fields; see its reference.

Preview deletion impact before selecting ordinary deletion, replacement, or cascade. Deleting definitions does not automatically stop remote processes or revoke remote keys. SD / internal-backup selection replaces the configuration set; use automation.config.preview / apply rather than overwriting protected files.

WebSocket integration

Connect to ws://10.10.99.97/ws, replacing the address with your device IP. This channel provides telemetry, logs, controller commands, and interactive SSH. A successful connection alone does not authorize private functions.

Authenticate and subscribe

Obtain token through HTTP login, then send:

{"type":"auth","token":"YOUR_TOKEN"}

Wait for auth_ok; failure returns auth_error. Ordinary telemetry topics are currently public, but establishing authentication remains useful for protected functions. Authentication cannot elevate a READ session to ROOT.

{"type":"subscribe","topic":"fan.status","params":{"interval":5000}}

Successful acknowledgement:

{"type":"subscribed","topic":"fan.status","success":true}

Illustrative data envelope:

{"type":"data","topic":"fan.status","timestamp":123,"data":{"fans":[]}}

timestamp is seconds since start; HTTP measurements and logs may use milliseconds. Subscription success is not proof that the first reading has arrived. If updates stop, inspect channel / source state and use HTTP readback as needed.

Topics

TopicDefault / minimum display intervalContent
system.dashboard1000 mscpu / memory / info / network / power / fan / services; unavailable sections may be omitted
system.info5000 msController information
system.memory5000 msController memory
system.cpu1000 msController CPU
network.status5000 msNetwork status
power.status5000 msPower status
fan.status5000 msFans
service.list5000 msController services
device.statusEvent-driven, default 2000 msComputer state events, not a periodic complete snapshot
ota.progressEvent-driven, default 1000 msDevice-wide progress; check HTTP progress and the version after restart
config.pack.validatedEvent-driven, default 0Uploaded package validation, not configuration application

params.interval is a nonnegative integer in milliseconds. The first eight periodic topics reject0 and raise smaller intervals to their minimum. An interval does not convert the last three event topics into polling. Re-subscribing to the same topic on a connection updates that subscription; it does not create a history queue.

Unsubscribe with {"type":"unsubscribe","topic":"fan.status"} and inspect unsubscribed / success. {"type":"ping"} receives pong. Pong does not establish session authorization or healthy telemetry.

Logs

ADMIN or higher is required. Authenticate, then send log_subscribe. History also requires ADMIN.

Outgoing typeFieldsResult / effect
log_subscribeminLevel, default VERBOSElog_subscribed / minLevel, then type=log
log_set_levelminLevelChanges this connection's filter, not all module output levels
log_get_historylimit default 500; minLevel ERROR; maxLevel VERBOSElog_history with logs / total, bounded by buffer capacity
log_unsubscribeNoneStops this connection's log stream

Log entries contain timestamp in milliseconds since start, level, levelName, tag, message, and task. Levels 0-5 are NONE / ERROR / WARN / INFO / DEBUG / VERBOSE. Retention is bounded; reconnect does not automatically replay history.

Controller command terminal

This terminal controls the management controller, not the Linux system on either computer. ROOT is required and commands can change hardware / configuration.

Outgoing typeFieldsResult
terminal_starttokenBinds and requests the terminal; connected includes prompt; occupancy returns terminal_busy / retry_after
terminal_inputdata: complete command stringoutput / data messages, then done with code / output_incomplete / stopped
terminal_interruptNoneRequests interruption; command_stopping may precede done
terminal_stopNoneReleases this connection's terminal, not a rollback of external effects

Only one terminal owner is active at a time. Do not take over a live terminal. Missing output does not by itself prove execution failure. Prefer structured HTTP state APIs over parsing terminal output for a first integration.

Interactive SSH Shell

ROOT is required. ssh_connect carries token and binds the connection. Verify remote fingerprints first; this Shell has no automatic unknown-fingerprint acceptance switch.

Outgoing typeFieldsResult
ssh_connecttoken, host, user; optional port22 / password for this remote loginssh_status connecting / connected / error; this entry uses password authentication
ssh_inputdataWrites text; explicitly include required newlines
ssh_resizewidth, heightIntegers1-65535 for terminal columns / rows
ssh_signalsignalSends a supported signal; unsupported requests fail
ssh_disconnectNoneDisconnects this connection's Shell; observe final ssh_status

Output uses ssh_output / data, status uses ssh_status / status / message. A connection controls only its own Shell. Do not replay input automatically after a failed control or disconnect; the remote side may have received it.

HTTP-started streaming SSH

Operational note

ssh.exec_stream starts through HTTP and returns session_id / boot_id / result_key. It is separate from the interactive Shell. Authenticate WebSocket before starting to avoid missing early events. Private events are delivered only to connections authorized for the initiating session.

Incoming typeFields and interpretation
ssh_exec_startsession_id, command and patterns; started, not completed
ssh_exec_outputsession_id, output_offset, output_length, is_stderr, data_b64
ssh_exec_matchsession_id, expect_matched / fail_matched, optional extracted / is_final
ssh_exec_runningIn-progress response from HTTP status query
ssh_exec_donesession_id, execution_status, exit_code, status / success and matches
ssh_exec_cancelledsession_id, execution_status; cancellation does not establish remote process termination
ssh_exec_errorsession_id, error, optional stage / detail

Decode data_b64 into bytes, verify output_length, and use output_offset to detect gaps / duplicates. Stream UTF-8 decoding across frames; characters can span messages.

Terminal results may include output_bytes / output_incomplete / collection_truncated / conditions_complete. Execution completion, condition matching, and output completeness are separate. exit_code=0 can coexist with missing output; incomplete matching is not a positive result. After disconnect, query ssh.exec_status with the receipt; it does not rerun the command or promise all historical output.

Capacity and reconnection

This build allows eight WebSocket clients and 32 topic subscriptions service-wide. Large frames, slow clients, exclusive tasks, and shutdown can reject work. Input must be protocol JSON text, at most 64 KiB; do not use fragmentation as a file-upload mechanism. JSON depth limits also apply.

Reconnect with delay, reauthenticate, and restore subscriptions. Do not automatically repeat terminal_input, ssh_input, or HTTP controls. Display last-update age and stale / disconnected state so old values do not appear current.

The companion subscribe.js example uses a browser that can reach the device and needs no third-party libraries.

File transfer and updates

Ordinary files and APP / WWW images use dedicated binary routes. Bodies contain original file bytes; successful responses do not necessarily include code. These routes are separate from the 277 logical API names.

Ordinary files

RouteMethod / accessRequest and result
/api/v1/file/downloadGET, READ; ADMIN for sensitive pathsAbsolute path in query; response is file bytes, not a directory
/api/v1/file/uploadPOST, ADMINDestination path in query, original bytes in body; success returns path / size / status=uploaded

HTTP uploads only allow validated ordinary files under /sdcard/. Other file operations, such as storage.rename / delete, have a different path scope; they do not allow HTTP upload to /spiffs/ or /www/. Sensitive configuration and private-key reads require ADMIN. Managed automation directories, aliases, backups, and temporary files remain protected; edit them through object configuration APIs.

Uploads allow at most 16 MiB with a 300-second receive budget, also limited by memory, free space, and storage state. Supply one complete nonempty file. Repeated requests do not append chunks. Upload replaces an existing destination; preserve needed content first. URL-encode paths once.

Operational note

Configure TS_BASE and TS_TOKEN before running:

curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 330 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  --data-binary @example.txt \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/file/upload?path=/sdcard/example.txt"

curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 60 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  --get --data-urlencode 'path=/sdcard/example.txt' \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/file/download" -o downloaded-example.txt

A .tscfg upload adds config_pack.valid / reason / signature information. uploaded means saved, not trusted or applied. Preview and apply through the object-specific import; config.pack.apply does not apply generic configuration. Ordinary data packages and command-bearing rule packages have different signing-usage checks; ordinary validation does not replace rule-import validation.

For file_replace_uncertain or a lost connection, inspect file metadata and download its contents before retrying.

Prepare images

Obtain a complete APP firmware image and matching www.bin for the hardware, partition layout, and firmware version. A WWW image is not an individual HTML file. Back up configuration, ensure stable power and a maintenance window, and prepare a recovery path.

Downloads accept HTTP and HTTPS. HTTPS uses system certificate trust by default. skip_verify is a download option; it cannot fix damaged or incompatible images or insufficient capacity. Normally keep it false. Current start APIs do not accept a private-CA cert_pem parameter.

Choose a transfer method

MethodAPIRequirements
Device downloadsota.start_url / ota.www.startDevice can reach the image server; check network and storage
SD fileota.start_file / ota.www.start_sdcardMounted SD with complete image files
Client uploadsDedicated binary routes belowClient has complete files; device has writable SD for staging and recovery cache
RouteMethod / accessOptions and success
/api/v1/ota/firmwarePOST, ADMINComplete APP body; auto_reboot query defaults true; status=success, size, message, reboot_pending, auto_reboot_requested
/api/v1/ota/wwwPOST, ADMINComplete www.bin body; status=success, size, message; no automatic restart

Both allow at most 16 MiB with a 300-second receive budget, subject to target-partition capacity and memory. Firmware headers and installation completeness are checked. Successful upload saves SD recovery files and a manifest with automatic recovery disabled; application acceptance after restart remains a separate step.

This example disables automatic restart so the maintenance process can inspect the result first:

curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 600 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  --data-binary @firmware.bin \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/ota/firmware?auto_reboot=false"

firmware.bin is a client-side filename; replace it with the complete firmware image. This request writes to the device. With auto_reboot=true, restart is requested about 2 seconds after a successful response and the connection may close.

Confirm progress and completion

After URL or SD initiation, read ota.progress, or ota.www.progress for WWW. Progress is device-wide without a private per-login task receipt. Coordinate updates through one maintenance process to avoid concurrent starts or cancelling another update.

curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/ota/progress"
Operational note

APP progress has state / percent / received_size / total_size / message. WWW uses received / total and adds running. pending_reboot means a restart is needed; error means failure. 100 percent alone does not prove the new version is running. To cancel, POST an empty object to ota.abort or ota.www.abort, then confirm state before starting again.

For binary uploads, use the HTTP response rather than assuming global progress identifies this request. HTTP409 with status=partial, error=recovery_cache_failed, and flash_written=true means Flash was written but the SD recovery cache was not fully saved. Inspect partitions and recovery files. A lost response also does not establish that no write occurred.

After firmware installation, restart as planned, log in again, inspect ota.status / partitions, and verify application health. ota.validate confirms the current firmware; call it after health checks.

Rollback and SD recovery

Check ota.partitions.can_rollback before ota.rollback. Rollback may restart immediately. Reconnect and verify version, configuration compatibility, and application state.

SD recovery uses TianShanOS.bin, www.bin, and manifest.json under /sdcard/recovery/. armed controls whether recovery is enabled; force controls version comparison. Existing files do not establish enabled recovery. Follow the publisher's recovery procedure because recovery affects a later boot and persistent storage; uploading files alone does not prove success.

No recovery preparation, status, or authorization API is exposed. Do not invent routes or treat ota.upload_begin / end / abort as a complete segmented-transfer protocol. Ordinary integrations should use the binary routes above.

Keep an integration running

Manage login state

Keep one session per client process and reuse it for requests. Schedule renewal from expires_in; log in again after a clear authentication failure rather than on every poll. There are eight session slots shared by scripts and browsers. When slots are full, a new login may invalidate an older session for the same account.

Normal sessions expire after 86400 seconds in this build. Restart, logout, password changes, and revocation require reauthentication. Treat tokens as opaque credentials, not values to parse or construct.

Poll or subscribe

Use HTTP for occasional reads and WebSocket for a continuously displayed dashboard. Subscribe only to required topics and unsubscribe when leaving a view. Display update intervals do not change hardware sampling or fan control periods.

After a disconnect, reconnect, authenticate, and restore subscriptions. Do not automatically repeat power commands, SSH execution, or updates. Telemetry and logs missed during disconnection are not guaranteed to be replayed.

Track one operation

Streaming SSH uses session_id+boot_id+result_key; the execution session_id differs from the login session_id. OTA uses device-wide progress without a private operation receipt.

SSH result queries require the complete receipt and initiating login; cancellation may use just the execution session_id from that same login. Do not share receipts. Restart, replacement, or limited retention can make results unavailable; inspect the remote state then. Coordinate OTA start, cancellation, and progress through one maintenance process, since global state is not an exclusive private task.

Timeouts and retries

Set connection and execution deadlines separately. Scans, network diagnostics, remote commands, and updates may take longer than ordinary reads. An HTTP timeout does not cancel server-side work.

Retry queries with bounded concurrency and increasing delay. For an uncertain write, inspect state first; repeat only when you know it did not start and still need it. Prefer an explicit desired state over toggle.

Configuration changes

Read active_version before writing and refresh after a conflict. Rules may also require expected_revision. Do not overwrite complete objects from a filtered list response.

Record application version, build date / time, and the capabilities used by your integration. Identical version strings can identify different repaired builds. After an upgrade, review method, role, field, and deprecation changes.

Operational records

Record time, target, operation type, business code, a brief reason, and non-secret operation identifiers. Store result credentials in controlled storage if retention is necessary. Ordinary logs should not contain Authorization, login bodies, private keys, or package secrets.

Troubleshooting

Record method, path, HTTP status, business code, reason, and operation receipt. Keep passwords, tokens, private keys, and full authorization headers out of support tickets.

Cannot connect

Use the current HTTP device address, such as http://10.10.99.97. The default port is80 and need not be written explicitly. Check the address, network reachability, and WebUI service state.

A working mTLS diagnostic page on443 does not prove the business API is running. Once the public system.info request works, investigate login and the target feature.

Authentication or permission failure

HTTP401 usually means a missing, invalid, or expired session;403 usually means insufficient privilege. Some handlers report authorization errors as business errors within HTTP200.

Log in again and inspect data.level. Admin can use ADMIN configuration and maintenance APIs; raw SSH execution, automation definition writes, and selected account management still require ROOT. Initial default passwords are rm01; use the current password if it has been changed. Password changes revoke affected sessions. Wait out login lockout instead of launching repeated concurrent retries.

Missing temperatures or telemetry

Inspect temp.sources for validity, update time, age, and source. Variable temperature input can be partly stale, so check valid weights / counts. monitor.data depends on a monitoring service on the compute host; inspect monitor connection and address configuration. Powered-on hardware does not guarantee telemetry has arrived.

Accepted but unfinished

Preserve and query the receipt or run record. SSH requires final status, exit code, and output completeness; managed services require verified state; OTA requires device-wide progress, partition state, and the running version after restart. started, cancel_requested, or a historical record alone is insufficient.

Configuration changed

For configuration_changed or a version conflict, reread current state and the relevant object. Compare and merge your unsaved input before submitting the new version. Do not simply replace the version token and repeat a delete / import / overwrite request.

Save failed or outcome unknown

Inspect applied, persisted, saved, uncertain, result_unknown, and the reason. Runtime state can change even when persistence fails. Read it back, then check saved startup configuration or backups as applicable. A network failure does not establish that the request had no effect.

SSH fingerprint changed

Stop automatic retries and obtain the current fingerprint from the server administrator. Check for reinstall, replacement, or address reassignment. Use the documented confirmation fields only after verification. An identical address does not guarantee the same host.

Busy or at capacity

Reduce concurrency, reuse sessions, and close unused subscriptions or terminals. Inspect active work. Tasks cannot queue indefinitely because a client keeps retrying. Wait for your own task's stop sequence; do not take over another connection's work.

Upload or update failed

Check role, complete request delivery, path, SD status, free capacity, target partition size, and complete images for the hardware / partition layout. Uploaded does not mean package validation or installation succeeded. For SSH, query the retained receipt; for OTA, inspect global progress and partition state before retrying, rolling back, or deleting recovery material.

Version and compatibility

This guide is based on TianshanOS 0.6.4. It remains useful for later versions where interfaces and procedures are unchanged. If parameters or results differ, follow the documentation for your installed version.

Connections and accounts

ItemUsage
Business APIHTTP, default port 80, prefix /api/v1; e.g. http://10.10.99.97
Live messagesWebSocket, ws://device-address / ws
Default accountsadmin / root, both initially rm01; use the current password if changed
Session authenticationLogin token in Authorization: Bearer
Access controlMinimum role per endpoint, with additional resource / version / ownership checks

Feature prerequisites

An available endpoint does not establish that all runtime dependencies are ready. Inspect the relevant status before use.

FeaturePrerequisites
Temperature, fans, power, computersInitialized drivers, existing targets, valid measurements
Compute telemetryRunning monitor, reachable host service, fresh valid data
Files and SD updatesRequired storage mounted, file present, sufficient capacity; direct upload has a separate flow
SSH / SFTP and managed servicesNetwork, credentials, host fingerprints, keys, saved configuration, task capacity
AutomationLoaded / enabled configuration, correct engine state, valid references, matching write versions
Configuration packagesDevice / recipient identity and publisher trust; export also requires Developer capability
Device PKI and updatesValid PKI material / time for diagnostics; complete compatible APP / WWW images for updates
Matrix contentSupported target and usable font / image files

Aliases and unsupported entries

config.pack.apply is retained but does not apply generic configuration; use the object-specific import. led.set writes pixel ranges. ota.upload_begin / end / abort control an upload, but no public upload_write data API is provided; ordinary integrations should use complete-image binary upload.

OTA retains upgrade_url / start_url and upgrade_file / start_file aliases. Prefer start_url / start_file for new integrations.

mTLS diagnostic service

This separate certificate-authenticated service defaults to 443. It is not another port for /api/v1. Availability depends on PKI material, configuration, and service state. Bearer tokens do not replace client certificates.

Method/pathMinimum certificate rolePurpose
GET /anonymousHealth
GET /api/auth/whoamiviewerCertificate identity
GET /api/test/viewerviewerRead-role test
GET /api/test/operatoroperatorOperator-role test
GET /api/test/adminadminAdmin read test
POST /api/test/admin-actionadminAdmin write test

These endpoints diagnose health, identity, and permissions rather than performing device business actions. Certificate viewer / operator / admin and business READ / ADMIN / ROOT belong to separate identity systems and cannot be interchanged.

Included examples

The PDF includes read_status.py and subscribe.js as attachments. Save them using a PDF reader that supports attachments; the editable companion contains the same files. Placeholder addresses, tokens, and certificate paths are not actual device settings.

Copy a code example

Code boxes contain selectable text without line numbers mixed into the code. To preserve indentation and line endings exactly, use the paperclip in the upper-right corner to save the named source file, or save it from your PDF reader's attachment panel.

If your reader does not support attachments, the download package contains all original examples in code-examples / en with matching filenames. Save API request JSON as request.json for the corresponding endpoint. Response examples and WebSocket messages serve the purposes described in their chapters. Fill in addresses, tokens, and other placeholders before use.

Python read-only query

Python 3 and its standard library are sufficient. Use your device address and run:

python3 read_status.py --base 'http://10.10.99.97' \
  --user admin

Enter the password at the hidden prompt rather than in command history. The script logs in, reads status, and attempts logout. It does not control hardware, run remote tasks, or upgrade. It follows no redirects and performs no automatic retries. Check valid / duty_valid and other measurement flags in its output.

Browser subscription

subscribe.js exports watchTianShan as an ES module without third-party libraries. Use a browser that can reach the device. Obtain a token through HTTP login first:

import {watchTianShan} from './subscribe.js';
const close = watchTianShan({
  baseUrl: 'http://10.10.99.97',
  token: yourLoginToken,
  onData: message => renderYourDashboard(message.data),
  onState: state => showConnectionState(state)
});

Your page supplies renderYourDashboard / showConnectionState. Call close() when leaving. Mark readings stale after disconnect before restoring authentication / subscriptions. Keep tokens out of source, URLs, and ordinary logs. The example does not reconnect automatically or replay actions.

Complete API index

All 277 registered names are included. Select a name to jump to an entry. Each entry lists the allowed methods, minimum access level, parameters, and checks for completion.

Send the reference request examples as POST JSON. Save an example as request.json, replace the placeholders, and call the listed path. Public calls may omit Authorization.

curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 60 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TS_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @request.json \
  "$TS_BASE/api/v1/PATH_FROM_REFERENCE"

Writes have real effects. Obtain the required versions, object IDs, certificates, or release materials first. Use GET only where it is explicitly allowed; use POST JSON for complex parameters.

auth.admin.reset_password

Restore the admin default password

Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/admin/reset_password Minimum access: ROOT

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
tokenstringRequiredValid login token in JSON; session_id is not a substitute.No default

Request example

{
  "token": "ROOT_TOKEN"
}

Response and completion

data.success / username / password_changed. After success, admin logs in with default password rm01.

Usage notes

Root restores the admin password to rm01. Use that default password after reset.

auth.admin.set_password

Root sets admin password

Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/admin/set_password Minimum access: ROOT

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
tokenstringRequiredValid login token in JSON; session_id is not a substitute.No default
new_passwordstringRequiredNew password, 4-64 bytes.No default

Request example

{
  "token": "ROOT_TOKEN",
  "new_password": "NEW_PASSWORD"
}

Response and completion

data.success / sessions_revoked / reauth_required / username / password_changed. Affected-account sessions are revoked.

Usage notes

Both the Authorization identity and the JSON token must pass root checks; both fields have a purpose.

auth.change_password

Change password

Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/change_password Minimum access: Body token (authentication-specific)

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
tokenstringRequiredValid login token in JSON; session_id is not a substitute.No default
old_passwordstringRequiredCurrent password.No default
new_passwordstringRequiredNew password, 4-64 bytes.No default

Request example

{
  "token": "YOUR_TOKEN",
  "old_password": "CURRENT_PASSWORD",
  "new_password": "NEW_PASSWORD"
}

Response and completion

data.success / sessions_revoked / reauth_required. Log in again after success.

Usage notes

The account holder chooses when to change the password. The old session is invalidated after success.

auth.login

User login

Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/login Minimum access: Public

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
usernamestringRequiredConfigured admin or root account.No default
passwordstringRequiredCurrent password for that account.No default

Request example

{
  "username": "admin",
  "password": "rm01"
}

Response and completion

POST success has code=0 and data.token / session_id / username / level / expires_in(seconds)/password_changed.

Usage notes

Five consecutive failures lock login for 300 seconds. Login does not establish WebSocket subscriptions.

auth.logout

User logout

Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/logout Minimum access: Body token (authentication-specific)

Parameters

No business parameters.

Request example

{}

Response and completion

Dedicated POST returns {success:true}. Also discard the client token.

Usage notes

Authorization identifies the session to close; no JSON is needed. The internal handler's body-token form is not the dedicated HTTP POST contract.

data.success / sessions_revoked / reauth_required / username / password_changed. Affected-account sessions are revoked.

Both the Authorization identity and the JSON token must pass root checks; both fields have a purpose.

auth.status

Check auth status

Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/status Minimum access: Body token (authentication-specific)

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted

data.id / points / applied / persisted.

ssh.cancel

Cancel running SSH exec session

Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/ssh/cancel Minimum access: ROOT

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted

Request example

  "session_id": 1
}

Requires the initiating login session; another root session cannot cancel it. A supplied receipt is still checked as a complete matching pair. cancelled acknowledges intent only; exec_status still needs the complete receipt.

ssh.exec

Execute remote command via SSH

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted

ssh.exec_status

Read owned current or latest SSH result

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted

result_keystringRequired32-character hexadecimal result credential from the receipt.No default

Request example

{
  "session_id": 1,
  "boot_id": "00000000000000000000000000000000",
  "result_key": "00000000000000000000000000000000"
}

Response and completion

data uses WebSocket result format: ssh_exec_running while active, ssh_exec_done / cancelled / error at termination. Check status / exit_code / success and output completeness.

Usage notes

Requires the initiating session and correct receipt. Zero-filled sample values show shape only; use the actual start response. Querying does not rerun the command.

ssh.exec_stream

Execute remote command with streaming output via WebSocket

Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/ssh/exec_stream Minimum access: ROOT

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
hoststringRequiredSSH host address.No default
userstringRequiredRemote username.No default
portintegerOptionalPort 1-65535.22
passwordstringAuthentication alternativePassword for this remote login, not the TianshanOS account.None
keyidstringAuthentication alternativeSaved SSH private-key ID on the device.None
commandstringRequiredCommand text.No default
expect_patternstringOptionalSuccess-match pattern.Unchanged
fail_patternstringOptionalFailure-match pattern.Unchanged
extract_patternstringOptionalOutput-extraction pattern.Unchanged
var_namestringOptionalResult-variable prefix.Unchanged
timeoutintegerOptionalMilliseconds here, unlike saved-command timeout_sec.Default execution deadline
collect_outputbooleanOptionalRetain collected output.true
max_output_sizeintegerOptionalOutput-collection limit in bytes.Device default
stop_on_matchbooleanOptionalStop after a match.false
command_idstringOptional pair with command_instanceAssociated saved-command ID.None
command_instancestringOptional pair with command_id16-character lowercase hexadecimal identity matching runtime_instance from the list.None

Request example

{
  "host": "192.0.2.20",
  "user": "YOUR_USER",
  "keyid": "example-key",
  "command": "uname -a",
  "collect_output": true
}

Response and completion

data.session_id / boot_id / result_key. Preserve the receipt before consuming WebSocket results or querying ssh.exec_status.

Usage notes

Exclusive streaming slot. No generic keypath authentication here. Verify ownership,terminal status,and output completeness.

passwordstringAuthentication alternativePassword for this remote login, not the TianshanOS account.None
keyidstringAuthentication alternativeSaved SSH private-key ID on the device.None
keypathstringSupported immediate-call authentication alternativeDevice private-key path; support varies by entry point.None
remotestringRequiredAbsolute remote file path.No default
localstringRequiredAbsolute local device file path.No default

Request example

{
  "host": "192.0.2.20",
  "user": "YOUR_USER",
  "keyid": "example-key",
  "remote": "/tmp/example.txt",
  "local": "/sdcard/example.txt"
}

Response and completion

data.remote / local / success; writes a remote file.

Usage notes

Requires verified remote host trust and authentication. Failures do not automatically accept fingerprints. get has local write restrictions; put sends local content remotely.

automation.proxy.fetch

Proxy fetch from external REST API

Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/automation/proxy/fetch Minimum access: READ

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
urlstringRequiredHTTP(S) destination or a supported local API address.No default
methodstringOptionalSupports GET / POST / PUT / DELETE; no generic request-body parameter.GET
headersobjectOptionalString-valued request headers; keep credentials out of ordinary logs.None
timeoutintegerOptionalTotal request timeout in milliseconds.15000
cert_pemstringOptionalPrivate-issuer CA material, at most 16384 bytes.System trust
skip_verifybooleanOptionalCompatibility parameter: false only; true is rejected.false

Request example

{
  "url": "https://example.com/status",
  "method": "GET"
}

Response and completion

data.status / content_length / body; local API results are nested in body, whose code must also be checked.

Usage notes

Local API forwarding retains the current session and destination permissions. External HTTP(S) requests require ROOT. Time, size, and network budgets apply; this is not an unrestricted proxy.

Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/automation/sources/add Minimum access: ROOT

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
idstringRequiredStable object ID; retain the existing ID after reading.No default
active_versionstringRequiredLatest active_version from configuration state; reread after changes.No default

See the shared data model.

Request example

{
  "id": "example-source",
  "label": "Temperature",
  "type": "rest",
  "enabled": false,
  "poll_interval_ms": 5000,
  "rest_url": "https://example.com/status",
  "rest_method": "GET",
  "auto_discover": false,
  "mappings": [
    {
      "path": "temperature",
      "var": "compute.temperature"
    }
  ],
  "active_version": "CURRENT_VERSION"
}

Response and completion

Configuration result with active_version / source / loaded / configured / enabled / paused / saved / uncertain and error location. See the complete config-result model.

Usage notes

Add requires an unused ID; update requires an existing object. See complete model examples.

automation.sources.add_mapping

Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/automation/sources/add_mapping Minimum access: ROOT

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
idstringRequiredStable object ID; retain the existing ID after reading.No default
active_versionstringRequiredLatest active_version from configuration state; reread after changes.No default
json_pathstringRequiredData field path to extract.No default
var_namestringRequiredDestination variable name.No default
transformstringOptionalOptional transform expression.None

See the shared data model.

Request example

{
  "id": "example-source",
  "active_version": "CURRENT_VERSION",
  "json_path": "temperature",
  "var_name": "compute.temperature"
}

Response and completion

Configuration-result model plus source_id / mapping_count / mapping_index.

automation.sources.delete

Delete a data source

Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/automation/sources/delete Minimum access: ROOT

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
idstringRequiredStable object ID; retain the existing ID after reading.No default
active_versionstringRequiredLatest active_version from configuration state; reread after changes.No default
previewbooleanOptionaltrue previews impact; false performs deletion.false
replacement_idstringOptionalReplacement object ID for dependent references.None
modestringOptionalcascade requests cascade handling; choose one strategy rather than combining force / replacement.Ordinary deletion
forcebooleanOptionalForce deletion of a referenced object only after previewing impact.false
pause_automationbooleanOptionalPause automation before handling.false

See the shared data model.

Request example

{
  "id": "example",
  "active_version": "CURRENT_VERSION",
  "preview": true
}

Response and completion

Configuration-result model plus impact describing references affected.

Usage notes

Deleting local definitions does not automatically stop remote programs or revoke public keys.

overwritebooleanOptionalPermit replacing an existing object with different content.false

}

led.set

Set an LED pixel range

Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/led/set Minimum access: ADMIN

Parameters

FieldTypeRequirementMeaningIf omitted
devicestringRequiredLED device name: touch / board / matrix; use led.list as authority.No default
colorstring / object / integerRequiredColor string, {r,g,b}, or a decimal 0xRRGGBB integer; components 0-255.No default
indexintegerOptionalZero-based first pixel; must be below the device pixel count.0
countintegerOptionalPositive number of consecutive pixels; the range must fit the device.1 with index; otherwise all pixels

Request example

{
  "device": "board",
  "index": 0,
  "count": 1,
  "color": {
    "r": 0,
    "g": 64,
    "b": 128
  }
}

Response and completion

data.device / start / count / color (r / g / b)/success.

Usage notes

Stops the target-layer animation and enables the device. Omitting index / count fills the whole device; index alone writes one pixel. A full fill updates the current solid-color preset. Persistent saving is a separate lighting-configuration step.

yintegerOptionalStarting vertical coordinate.Default position
